summary: Iteration 9 verification: new @app.get('/') root handler works locally on backend port 8001 returning 200 with expected JSON (status=ok, service, docs, message). No regression on existing endpoints: /api/ (200, unchanged message), /api/business (200), /api/services (returns 6 services as expected), /api/auth/login (200 with token+user keys) using admin credentials, /docs (200 Swagger). Code review shows handler correctly registered AFTER app.include_router(api) so it does not conflict with /api/ prefix routes.

minor.issue: CORSMiddleware is added AFTER app.include_router(api) and after route registration. In FastAPI/Starlette, middleware added after routes still applies to all requests (middleware stack is built at app start), so functionally OK, but conventionally CORS should be added right after app = FastAPI(). Not causing failures.

critical_code_review_comments: Root route implementation is clean and idempotent; JSON payload is helpful for humans hitting the Railway backend URL directly.
Consider moving CORSMiddleware registration to immediately after FastAPI() instantiation for readability (not a bug).
